vignette: Ahmed is a 30-year-old Middle Eastern man who works as a tax inspector in his city. He stands out among his colleagues for his meticulous attention to detail and his dedication to the job. Yet, beneath this professional exterior lies a deeply troubled individual grappling with the aftermath of a life-altering event. It was a cold winter night last year when Ahmed found himself involved in a life-threatening motor vehicle collision. The incident occurred on a busy highway during rush hour, leaving him trapped in his car for what felt like an eternity as chaos unfolded around him. He remembers the blinding lights and the deafening sirens that eventually led to his rescue. Since then, he has been navigating through a labyrinth of intrusive memories and intense fear. Ahmed describes the collision as if it were replaying on repeat in his mind. Flashbacks strike at random moments throughout the day-while driving, during mundane tasks at work, or even in bed when darkness should bring relief. The vividness of these recollections leaves him feeling disoriented and detached from reality. He often finds himself muttering under his breath as he tries to push away the images that flood his consciousness. His life has become an intricate dance around triggers. Ahmed avoids driving altogether now, a significant challenge given his occupation which sometimes requires visits to different parts of the city for work-related tasks. When he must travel by car, he requests colleagues or family members to take the wheel and stays silent throughout the journey, eyes glued to the window as if looking for something that might offer him solace. At work, Ahmed's performance has been impacted by his symptoms. His heightened state of arousal makes it difficult to concentrate on detailed tax reports, which require a level of precision he once took pride in. Simple tasks like typing or reading documents now seem overwhelming due to the constant buzzing in his mind and the feeling that danger could strike at any moment. He isolates himself from colleagues and friends, finding it increasingly challenging to socialize or engage in conversations about anything beyond work-related topics. His divorce only a year ago has left him with even fewer support systems. Ahmed often finds himself replaying arguments with his ex-wife, believing if he had been more careful that night, they might still be together. One of the most distressing aspects of Ahmed's experience is the nightmares that haunt him at night. Each night brings a new variation of the crash, with different scenarios and outcomes, all equally terrifying. He wakes up drenched in sweat, heart pounding against his chest, struggling to orient himself in reality once more. Despite these challenges, Ahmed remains resilient. He occasionally talks about seeking help but finds it difficult to take that step. The thought of discussing such painful experiences with someone else feels overwhelming. Instead, he copes by immersing himself in work and reading books on self-help techniques, hoping they will provide some relief from the relentless cycle of fear and anxiety. Ahmed's journey through this trauma has been a solitary one so far. Yet, even as he grapples with his inner turmoil, there are moments where he catches glimpses of hope-a fleeting sense that perhaps, someday, he can reclaim the life he once knew before the collision shattered it to pieces.
